proposed.content:
Final output guard — fires last, immediately before emitting JSON:
1. JSON SYNTAX — Scan all string fields in your output for unescaped backslashes. Common sources: LaTeX (\frac, \pi, \(, \), \text, \mathbb), code escapes, file paths. Replace all technical notation with plain-text equivalents in your output (write F_S(s) not \(F_S(s)\); write pi not \pi; write 1/(r^2 s^2) not \frac{1}{r^2 s^2}). Also check for unescaped double-quotes inside strings. Invalid JSON = total failure regardless of analysis quality.
2. COUNT CHECK — Your ratings array length must equal N from your perception scan. If shorter, you skipped candidates — go back and evaluate them.
3. PERCEPTION-ERROR SCAN — If your reasoning contains phrases like 'could not locate,' 'not real candidates,' 'part of the playbook,' 'no candidate content,' or 'missing data,' you have a perception error. Re-read the full input from the beginning and redo your evaluation. Candidates are always present.
proposed.rationale: Both math:796 rollouts scored 0% because the agent's reasoning contained raw LaTeX backslashes (e.g., \(F_S(s)\)) making the JSON output unparseable. The existing guard checks semantic properties but never validates JSON syntax, providing false safety. Adding JSON syntax validation as step 1 addresses this deterministic total-failure mode that generalizes to any domain with special characters.

proposed.content:
Step one — mandatory constraint extraction. Fires UNCONDITIONALLY, immediately after the perception scan, BEFORE any domain analysis.

ARTIFACT GATE: Your reasoning MUST begin with a labeled CONSTRAINT CHECKLIST block. No evaluation prose, domain analysis, or candidate scoring may precede it.

CONSTRAINT CHECKLIST procedure:
1. EXTRACT — Read the FULL prompt. List every discrete requirement as a numbered item: content/topic, format/structure, quantitative constraints, stylistic directives.
2. TUNNEL-VISION WARNING: In domain tasks (code, math, science), non-domain constraints (sentence ratios, word counts, formatting rules) are the most frequently missed and most likely decisive differentiator.
3. VALIDATE — Confirm each item is a genuine stated requirement, not a formatting artifact.

EVALUATE — For each candidate, assign Pass/Partial/Fail on every checklist item. Write this compliance matrix before scoring.

COUNTING RULE with ENFORCEMENT: For countable constraints ('at least N,' 'exactly N,' '2:1 ratio,' word/sentence limits), a Pass or Fail verdict is BLOCKED until your reasoning contains an explicit COUNTING ARTIFACT for that candidate — enumerate each counted item with identifying context, state the computed total, and compare numerically to the target. Qualitative substitutes ('many,' 'several,' 'has questions') are BANNED. If you wrote a verdict without the artifact, reclassify as UNCHECKED and redo. Never reduce a quantitative constraint to a binary present/absent check.

HARD GATE: For mechanically verifiable constraints, Pass/Fail takes absolute precedence. No FAILing candidate may outscore a PASSing one. Exception: factual accuracy.

ALL-FAIL TIEBREAK: Before declaring all-fail, produce a per-candidate table (candidate | measured | target | distance). Proximity wins; content tiebreaking only when distances are indistinguishable.

INDEPENDENT SELF-AUDIT: After scoring, re-read the original prompt from scratch. List every explicit constraint you find. Confirm each appears in your checklist and was evaluated for every candidate. If any is missing, redo before finalizing.
proposed.rationale: In precise_if:575 (both rollouts), the agent wrote 'Pass all' on the 2:1 ratio constraint without producing any counting artifact — reducing a quantitative ratio to a binary presence check. This is a persistent failure (iterations 5,7,9,10,13,14). The existing COUNTING RULE mandates an artifact but has no enforcement gate catching when the verdict is issued without it. Adding BLOCKED-until-artifact-exists and explicit reclassification of unsupported verdicts as UNCHECKED provides the missing enforcement mechanism.

proposed.content:
CROSS-CANDIDATE COMPARISON: When candidates share structural similarity (same sources cited, overlapping claims, parallel format), produce a DIFF TABLE before scoring — rows = shared items (cited sources, attributed quotes, specific claims), columns = candidates. Mark each row AGREE or CONTRADICT.

MANDATORY TRIGGER: When 2+ candidates attribute specific content (quotes, definitions, statistics) to the same named source, the DIFF TABLE must be built BEFORE any relative scoring. Do not skip this step.

CORROBORATION (agree): If 2+ candidates converge on a specific claim, classify it as 'corroborated' — require a concrete counter-fact (per ISOLATE→COUNTER) before applying any fabrication penalty.

ANTI-CORROBORATION (contradict): If candidates attribute different specific content to the same source, at least one must be wrong. Flag all contradicted items as UNVERIFIED. Never resolve by subjective plausibility ('feels more standard,' 'more coherent'). Either verify with a concrete counter-fact, or treat all versions as equally suspect. A candidate whose primary advantage rests on unverified contradicted claims must not outscore one with fewer but uncontradicted claims.

ALL-UNVERIFIABLE CEILING: When ALL candidates' primary differentiating content is UNVERIFIED or UNVERIFIABLE (e.g., all attributed quotes are unconfirmable), no candidate gets a factuality advantage from that content. Differentiate by secondary verifiable signals: prompt-constraint compliance, internal consistency, appropriate hedging. Subjective presentation quality ('cleaner,' 'more professional') alone cannot separate candidates by more than 0.3 points.
proposed.rationale: In factuality:201 (both rollouts identical), candidates [1] and [4] attributed different quotes to the same six authors. The agent never built a DIFF TABLE, noted all quotes were unverifiable, then used 'cleaner presentation' to rank incorrect [4] above correct [1]. Adding a mandatory trigger for same-source attribution and an all-unverifiable ceiling prevents presentation quality from serving as a prohibited tiebreaker when no factual differentiation is possible.
